Description

Amazon is continuing to invest in the measurement of its ads products in order to tap into the growing digital advertising marketplace. Amazon Ads' Measurement, AdTech and Data Science (MADS) team is looking for an experienced Senior Manager, Software Development to lead engineering teams building our Performance Measurement systems.

You will own engineering teams responsible for how advertisers measure the performance of their ad campaigns, combining deterministic approaches with modeled approaches to deliver a complete and trustworthy view of advertising outcomes across channels, devices, and the full customer journey.

This role is at the intersection of big data systems engineering, applied science, and advertiser-facing product delivery. You will lead 30-50 engineers across multiple teams, owning petabyte-scale data pipelines that process billions of events daily, real-time and batch attribution systems, experimentation infrastructure (randomized controlled trials at scale), and privacy-preserving measurement architectures. Your systems directly inform how advertisers allocate billions in ad spend.

You think big, have a bias for action, and bring a history of delivering results in complex distributed systems environments. You thrive in ambiguity and are ready to scale advertising measurement. You are equally comfortable diving deep into system architecture as you are setting multi-year technical strategy with senior leadership.

The right candidate will possess a strong engineering leadership background, will have demonstrated experience building and operating large-scale data and ads systems, and will have a well-rounded understanding of advertising, causal inference, and privacy-constrained computation. You must be able to thrive and succeed in an entrepreneurial environment, and not be hindered by ambiguity or competing priorities. This means you are not only able to develop and drive high-level technical strategy, but can also roll up your sleeves, dive deep into system designs, and unblock your teams when it matters.

You set technical direction, define system architectures, partner deeply with scientists to translate research into production-grade systems, and build engineering organizations that deliver at high velocity. You will work directly with product managers, scientists, and cross-functional teams to define solutions that balance measurement precision with system latency, privacy constraints, and advertiser trust. You drive prioritization, make build-vs-buy decisions, own operational excellence for mission-critical systems, and develop engineering talent across multiple locations.

You will also drive AI-native development practices across your organization, leveraging agentic AI tooling to accelerate engineering velocity, automate operational workflows, and fundamentally rethink how measurement systems are built and maintained. We expect leaders in this role to be hands-on adopters who push their teams toward AI-augmented development as the default.

jobs.title: Director, AWS Catalog
jobs.description:
Description

The AWS data catalog is how customers find, understand, and govern their data on AWS. The AWS Glue Data Catalog is the metadata layer beneath AWS analytics. It holds the schemas, table definitions, and partitions that Athena, EMR, Redshift, Glue, and SageMaker need to plan and execute a query, which puts it in the data path of nearly every analytical workload our customers run, and its crawlers are how a large share of that metadata gets discovered and kept current in the first place. Alongside it, AWS Lake Formation governs fine-grained access to that data, and Amazon DataZone provides the business context, discovery, and lineage (domains, projects, and data products) that make a data estate comprehensible to the people and applications using it. Together these three services serve customers of every size, from day-one startups to the largest enterprises in the world, and hold the definitive record of the data those customers store in Amazon S3 and query with our engines. We are investing heavily to make working with that data dramatically simpler for customers, and to ensure the catalog operates at the hyperscale we expect AI agents, rather than people, to drive as they become the primary consumers of enterprise data. Catalogs have become the control point for enterprise data and AI, and we are at the very beginning of building the one customers standardize on.

As a Director of Software Development for the AWS Catalog organization, you will lead a group of top talent building the metadata, governance, and discovery layer for all data on AWS. You will own the AWS Glue Data Catalog and its crawlers, AWS Lake Formation, and Amazon DataZone, and you will drive the roadmap and deliver on three fronts at once: building a foundation that operates at a scale and request rate well beyond what any catalog handles today, with the availability and latency that every analytics service above you depends on; making governance simpler and stronger for customers who have to know and prove who can see what across a large data estate; and making the catalog the layer that AI agents reason through, with the discovery, semantic search, and business metadata that let an agent find the right data without being told where it lives. You will do this while holding a deep commitment to open standards, building on Apache Iceberg and the Iceberg REST Catalog and interoperating with third-party catalogs rather than locking customers in. You'll lead multiple engineering teams through managers across geographic locations, and you'll spearhead new technologies that change what a catalog is capable of. You'll be a leader in the business as well, owning the financial health and growth of your services. You'll personally engage with C-suite customers to represent AWS's data catalog strategy.

Success in this role requires a leader experienced in establishing and building relationships with a wide range of peers, including senior AWS executives, customers at all levels of experience and responsibility, deeply technical software and systems engineers within the team, and internal organizations. Because the catalog sits between storage and every analytics and AI service, this role rewards a leader who builds strong partnerships across engineering teams and brings them along behind a shared technical direction. This leader must have the proven skills to easily switch between weighing in on complex engineering details, taking a long-term view of the business, growing and developing the next generation of AWS leadership, and overall operating as a large-scale organization leader. It requires the judgment to balance urgent, high-value customer features against multi-year foundational investment, and the discipline to evolve a large and sophisticated installed base without disruption, for customers whose compliance posture depends on us. It requires an ability to prioritize work for the direct team and partner teams, establish goals, and focus attention on the most important inputs to drive the desired business outcomes. This leader must be capable of scaling themselves and their team to meet the ever-increasing demands of a fast-growing business, and will excel at hiring and developing technical talent. The catalog is in the path of every query our customers run, so a passion and discipline around operational excellence is essential. Come build the catalog that every engine and every agent on AWS reasons through.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience)

15+ years of software development experience

10+ years in senior engineering leadership roles

Preferred Qualifications

Background in data analytics, engines and catalogs.

Proven experience scaling large engineering organizations across multiple geographies.

Track record of delivering customer-facing products with high velocity in a fast-moving, competitive landscape.

Experience leading product engineering, from ideation through design, build, deploy, and support.

Description

How would you like to be a part of Earth’s most customer-centric company? You would work with teams of front-line responders who support the operations of some of the world’s most powerful data centers. Our Data Center Engineering Operations team maintain and operate our critical infrastructure systems so that they are prepared to stand up against any situation.

AWS has the world’s largest cloud computing portfolio. As an Amazonian you will work in some of the most sophisticated, safe, and secure data centers in the world. Our Chief Engineers (CE) help keep them that way by working with the brightest minds from around the globe to help test and implement the newest technology and work practices to meet the demands of a changing market.

We have a passion for learning and evolving, it’s how we have helped define ourselves as leaders in the industry. Let’s work hard, have fun, and make history!

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Key job responsibilities

Act as the primary escalation point for all facilities-related issues. Oversee operation and management of routine and emergency services on a variety of critical systems such as: switchgear, generators, UPS systems, power distribution equipment, chillers, cooling towers, computer room air handlers, building monitoring systems, etc.

This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

The CE directs, trains and supports technicians in their role of providing hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting and operations. Implementation and execution of site/equipment-specific training exercises is also expected. They manage projects from conception to completion. These projects involve independent work as well as collaboration with external support groups including engineering, automation, processing, and finance in both local and global settings. and scales new infrastructure technologies from concept through global fleet deployment. The

platforms, power densities, cooling technologies, and emerging infrastructure requirements on

across OCI's global footprint. The organization will develop standardized engineering processes

management, commissioning, and operational handoff while ensuring engineering decisions are

Partner with Design Engineering, OEMs, Product Engineering, and Supply Chain to

engineering and construction activities from the field into manufacturing environments through

Lead joint product development initiatives that deliver differentiated infrastructure

Establish engineering engagement models supporting product qualification, validation,

Job Description

Oracle is seeking a Senior Manager, Supply Chain Engineering to lead the Component Quality Engineering organization supporting Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) hardware platforms.

This management role sits within the Quality organization and is responsible for building and leading the team that manages silicon suppliers and other critical component commodities used across complex AI infrastructure, server, storage, networking, and rack-level hardware products.

The leader will own quality execution across key commodities including GPUs, CPUs, memory, storage, networking, optics, interconnects, power, PCBs, thermal components, and L6 components. This role will connect supplier quality, component engineering, factory quality, field reliability, failure analysis, and root cause and corrective action (RCCA) execution into a clear quality operating model for critical hardware ramps.

This leader will build the team, establish operating discipline, and ensure component quality risks are identified early, effectively contained, and driven to closure with suppliers, sub-tier suppliers, manufacturing partners, and Oracle engineering teams.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Lead the Component Quality Engineering organization responsible for critical silicon and hardware commodities across OCI infrastructure programs.
Build, manage, mentor, and develop a team of component quality engineers.
Own supplier-facing component quality strategy and execution, including supplier metrics, failure trends, RCCA quality, corrective action validation, and escalation management.
Manage quality engagement with silicon and critical commodity suppliers across GPUs, CPUs, memory, storage, networking, optics, interconnects, power, thermal, PCBs, and L6 components.
Drive component-level failure analysis and RCCA coordination for factory, integration, field, RMA, repair, NCAT, and SSP issues.
Establish clear supplier quality expectations, including DPPM, RPM, AFR/RMA performance, MTBF expectations, containment discipline, 8D quality, PCN review rigor, and corrective action effectiveness.
Partner with factory quality, process quality, manufacturing, test, design engineering, sourcing, planning, repair, and field teams to connect component issues to outgoing quality and field reliability risk.
Ensure component quality risks are clearly represented in OK-to-Ramp and OK-to-Ship reviews, including open supplier issues, containment status, test coverage gaps, field exposure, and residual risk.
Create and maintain component quality risk registers for critical programs and suppliers, with clear ownership, due dates, containment status, and decision recommendations.
Support NPI and production-ramp readiness by reviewing qualification data, supplier process controls, PCNs, alternate-source plans, supplier capacity changes, and new technology risks.
Lead cross-functional task forces for high-impact supplier or component quality issues, ensuring clear problem statements, current data, effective containment, and technically credible RCCA.
Provide concise executive-level communication on supplier quality risks, field reliability trends, manufacturing impact, recovery plans, and recommended actions.
Develop engineers to strengthen technical depth, supplier influence, quality judgment, executive communication, and cross-functional leadership.

Required Skills And Experience

Experience leading teams within component quality, supplier quality, hardware quality, reliability engineering, manufacturing quality, or supply chain engineering.
Strong understanding of semiconductor, server, storage, networking, power, thermal, or other high-complexity hardware component quality.
Demonstrated ability to manage suppliers and sub-tier suppliers through containment, failure analysis, RCCA, corrective action validation, and quality improvement.
Strong working knowledge of quality and reliability metrics including DPPM, RPM, AFR, RMA, MTBF, yield, retest rate, failure pareto, and escape risk.
Experience supporting NPI, production ramp, sustaining quality, field failure reduction, supplier escalations, and customer-impacting quality issues.
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional problem solving across engineering, manufacturing, test, sourcing, planning, repair, field teams, and external suppliers.
Strong decision-making skills under ambiguity, particularly when quality data is incomplete and product delivery pressure is high.
Strong communication skills, including the ability to brief senior leaders on risk, impact, recovery plans, and decision tradeoffs.
Experience hiring, developing, and leading engineers in a fast-paced technical organization.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AI infrastructure, GPU platforms, rack-scale systems, servers, storage systems, networking infrastructure, or large-scale data center hardware.
Experience managing quality for silicon suppliers and critical component commodities such as GPUs, CPUs, memory, SSDs, NICs, switches, optics, cables, power supplies, PDUs, fans, PCBs, or L6 components.
Experience applying structured RCCA and quality methods including 8D, 5-Why, Fishbone, CAPA, DOE, FMEA, SPC, MSA, control plans, and supplier audits.
Experience building a new team, scaling operating cadence, and defining quality ownership across a growing organization.
Six Sigma, CQE, CRE, Lean, or equivalent quality and reliability training.

What Success Looks Like

In this role, you will:

Establish clear commodity ownership, supplier engagement cadence, issue escalation paths, and measurable quality metrics across the Component Quality Engineering organization.
Ensure critical component quality issues have effective containment, technically credible RCCA, validated corrective actions, and clear factory and field exposure assessments.
Create visibility into supplier quality performance through DPPM, RPM, AFR/RMA, failure pareto, PCN risk, and corrective action closure metrics.
Bring a clear component quality risk view into OK-to-Ramp and OK-to-Ship decisions, including supplier readiness, containment status, test coverage, and residual risk.
Build an organization capable of supporting high-priority hardware ramps while identifying and addressing quality risks early with clear ownership.
Develop engineers into strong technical owners who can lead task forces, challenge weak RCCA, and clearly communicate quality risk to executive stakeholders.

The AWS data catalog is how customers find, understand, and govern their data on AWS. The AWS Glue Data Catalog is the metadata layer beneath AWS analytics. Together these three services serve customers of every size, from day-one startups to the largest enterprises in the world, and hold the definitive record of the data those customers store in Amazon S3 and query with our engines. We are investing heavily to make working with that data dramatically simpler for customers, and to ensure the catalog operates at the hyperscale we expect AI agents, rather than people, to drive as they become the primary consumers of enterprise data. Catalogs have become the control point for enterprise data and AI, and we are at the very beginning of building the one customers standardize on.

You will own the AWS Glue Data Catalog and its crawlers, AWS Lake Formation, and Amazon DataZone, and you will drive the roadmap and deliver on three fronts at once: building a foundation that operates at a scale and request rate well beyond what any catalog handles today, with the availability and latency that every analytics service above you depends on; making governance simpler and stronger for customers who have to know and prove who can see what across a large data estate; and making the catalog the layer that AI agents reason through, with the discovery, semantic search, and business metadata that let an agent find the right data without being told where it lives. Oracle is seeking a Senior Manager, Supply Chain Engineering to lead the Component Quality Engineering organization supporting Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) hardware platforms.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Lead the Component Quality Engineering organization responsible for critical silicon and hardware commodities across OCI infrastructure programs.
Build, manage, mentor, and develop a team of component quality engineers.
Own supplier-facing component quality strategy and execution, including supplier metrics, failure trends, RCCA quality, corrective action validation, and escalation management.
